title: Video compression for spatiotemporal Earth system data
author: Pellicer-Valero O., Aybar C. and Camps-Valls G.
abstract: Large-scale Earth system datasets — from high-resolution remote sensing imagery to spatiotemporal climate model outputs — exhibit spatial, temporal, and spectral redundancies that make them natural candidates for video compression. We present xarrayvideo, a Python library that compresses multichannel spatiotemporal Earth system data (ESD) by encoding them as videos via ffmpeg: spectral bands are mapped to color channels, and time steps to video frames, while non-video metadata is stored in a companion NetCDF file. Our core contribution is not a new codec, but a practical interoperability layer that makes decades of optimized video engineering immediately applicable to ESD. We demonstrate compression ratios of up to 250× with very high reconstruction fidelity across four representative datasets spanning EO imagery (DynamicEarthNet, DeepExtremeCubes, SimpleS2) and reanalysis fields (ERA5). Compressed versions of DynamicEarthNet (525GB→8.5GB at 76.63 dB PSNR) and DeepExtremeCubes (2.3 TB→323GB at 67.81 dB PSNR) are openly released in the FAIR-compliant TACO v2 format on HuggingFace. Downstream deep learning performance (land-cover segmentation and next-step reflectance prediction) shows no degradation on the compressed datasets at the quality levels evaluated. Overall, xarrayvideo provides a practical, zero-training solution to the growing storage challenges in Earth system sciences, built on standard, hardware-accelerated video tooling. The library is available at https://github.com/IPL-UV/xarrayvideo.
